The rebound lab / F04 + F07

Cheaper tasks.
More energy, or less?

An explorer for the conditional demand–energy identity in P05 and the three futures named in P08. Every number here comes from declared assumptions about an abstract, illustrative indexed workload—not from company data, measured elasticities, or forecasts.

Method / one shared identity

Declared assumptions in. Indexed results out.

S1/S0 = q^(−e)
Successful demand responds to the price ratio q = P1/P0.
A = S / s
Attempts; each retry counts once as an attempt.
E = A × I × p
Facility kWh = attempts × IT kWh per attempt × PUE.
E1/E0 = q^(−e) × k
k = (s0/s1) × (I1/I0) × (p1/p0), the effective intensity ratio.
e* = ln(k) / ln(q)
Break-even elasticity magnitude, defined for q ≠ 1 and k > 0.

Routed futures partition successful demand with shares that sum to 1, then apply each route’s success rate and intensity: k = Σ share × k(route). Results agree within relative 1e-9 (absolute floor 1e-12).

What this lab is—and is not

No company calibration: filing claims are located but unverified (T-014 awaits review), and no Anthropic, OpenAI, or provider figure enters any input. The workload is an abstract illustrative indexed workload until the coding, extraction, and agent rubrics (T-005) are reviewed.

Indexed baseline = 100. Absolute kWh appear only from all three baseline values you enter; missing values stay unknown, never zero. Deterministic: no seed and no Monte Carlo (T-031 is later work).

A price ratio is not a margin, and an energy index is not an efficiency score; financial and physical measures stay separate. Not yet reviewed.

F04 / Elasticity threshold · P05

Where cheaper becomes more.

Below the threshold e*, induced demand is too weak to offset lower energy per successful task, so facility energy falls. Above it, demand outruns efficiency and energy rises. The threshold moves whenever success, intensity, or PUE changes.

Illustrative indexed scenario — not calibrated, not a forecast

Declared conditions

Defaults reproduce the P05 proportional case: price and IT energy per attempt both halve (g = 0.5) with success and PUE unchanged, so e* = 1.

Positive. 0.5 halves the price per successful task.

0 < s ≤ 1. Attempts = successful tasks ÷ s.

0 < s ≤ 1. Retries count once each as attempts.

Positive. Facility overhead relative to baseline.

Static reference · the P05 proportional case

Computed at build time with task-energy/0.4.0 for q = 0.5 and k = 0.5: price and IT energy per attempt both halve while success and PUE stay fixed. It does not change with your edits and stays readable without JavaScript. Here E1/E0 = g^(1−e) with g = 0.5, so energy falls for e < 1, is unchanged at e = 1, and rises for e > 1. This is a conditional identity (CL-013), not an elasticity estimate.

F07 / Scenario comparison · P08

Three futures, one identity.

Each future declares price, elasticity, success, intensity, and—for substitution—routing assumptions for the same abstract workload. Edit any input: results, comparison, and sensitivity update together. Invalid inputs withhold results rather than guess.

Illustrative indexed scenario — not calibrated, not a forecast

F07 · Scenario comparison. Indexed successful tasks, attempts, and facility energy (baseline = 100) for three declared futures, with each future’s threshold e* and an elasticity sensitivity sweep. Run manifest · export and replay

A manifest records schema, model and paper versions, the evidence cutoff (none (indexed)), all inputs, results, and tolerance (relative 1e-9). Import replays it and requires the recorded results to reproduce; a rejected file leaves the current run unchanged. Files are read locally and never uploaded.

Imported text is treated as data: strict fields, finite numbers, known scenario and route references.
